whole_work_scope.recommendation: Approve ONE canonical poem identity, efchad_bemaasai, in ONE complete file with 46 strophes in source order: 30 strophes for the letters א–ס, then 2 each for ע, פ, צ, ק, ר, ש, ת, then the second ת pair. Eight of the Shabbat ten verses, each with its recitation formula, sit between strophe groups as bounded quote contexts carrying Bible @source: Gen 8:1 after strophe 30, Ps 111:4–5, Mal 3:16, Ex 2:24, Ps 105:8, Jer 2:2, Ex 32:13, Ps 74:2. Do not use canonical Bible verse milestones there. The poem file ends with strophe 46 (תְּרַפֵּק … חַקֹּתָ לְזִכָּרוֹן). One change to the proposal: the last Shabbat formula, 'כַּכָּתוּב עַל יַד נְבִיאֶךָ', goes in the Shabbat branch of the structural file, directly after the Efchad transclusion and not inside the poem file. Its verse, Jer 31:19, is printed only once, full width and shared by both branches. This matches the weekday branch, which also ends on its own lead-in ('וְנֶאֱמַר') before the same shared verse. Put the weekday/Shabbat choice once, in the structural file, starting at Atah Zokher /opening. Weekday branch: zekher_techillat (complete poem file, 44 strophes), then Atah Zokher /vegam_et_noach, then the weekday verse series ending 'וְנֶאֱמַר'. Shabbat branch: Atah Zokher /vegam_et_noach, then the efchad_bemaasai file, then 'כַּכָּתוּב עַל יַד נְבִיאֶךָ'. Both branches then join at the shared Jer 31:19, the petition, the optional brit stanza and the conclusion. Never interleave by page or region. The eight incipits (aseh_fela, peneh_elohim, …, tar_ish_tam) are not poem identities. At most they are strophe or section labels inside efchad_bemaasai.
evidence: Layout, s278: only one Shabbat heading ('אַם שַׁבָּת') and one attribution, 'מיוסד ע״פ א״ב כפול בראשי החרוזות', come before strophe 1. On s284, s286, s288 and s290 the eight later pieces have no heading, attribution, title or new ק׳ opening label. The 'אַם שַׁבָּת' at the top of each page is a running region label. It also appears on s282, inside the 30-strophe section, so it does not mark a new poem.

Speaker labels run straight through: ח׳ first appears before strophe 30 (סוֹגֵר), which is the second strophe of the ס pair. After that, every pair has ח׳ before its second strophe (עוֹרַרְתָּ, פָּעֳלָם, צְרָרוּם, קַהְתָּה, רָצָה, שֶׁכָּלוּ, תְּמוּר, תְּרַפֵּק). The ס pair and the 'short pieces' use one alternation pattern, so they are one performance unit. None of the pieces restarts with its own ק׳.

Same verse form throughout: every strophe from 1 to 46 has four cola and ends on the זִכָּרוֹן refrain (לְזִכָּרוֹן / וְזִכָּרוֹן / מִזִּכָּרוֹן, e.g. 'כִּי שְׁכַחְנוּ מִזִּכָּרוֹן'). The type size is the same as strophes 1–30.

Acrostic: 15 letters (א–ס) × 2 = 30, then ע–ת, 7 letters × 2 = 14, giving 44, which completes the 'א״ב כפול'. The added ת pair (תָּר אִישׁ תָּם / תְּרַפֵּק) makes 46. The attribution only promises a double alphabet. The extra ת pair has the same form and labels and no heading, so it reads as a closing extension, not a separate work.

The verses belong to the piyyut's own design. The Shabbat verses are not the standard Zikhronot ten. Mal 3:16, Ps 105:8, Ex 32:13 and Ps 74:2 replace Lev 26:42, Ps 106:45 and Ezek 16:60. They follow a Torah–Writings–Prophets cycle three times (Gen 8:1 | Ps 111:4, 111:5 | Mal 3:16 || Ex 2:24 | Ps 105:8 | Jer 2:2 || Ex 32:13 | Ps 74:2 | Jer 31:19), which makes ten verses, with Jer 31:19 as the tenth.

Each strophe group points ahead to its verse. סוֹגֵר דֶּלֶת בְּעַד תְּמִימִים (Noah in the ark) leads to Gen 8:1. תַּעַשׂ לְזִכָּרוֹן / לְנִפְלְאוֹתֶיךָ leads to 'זֵכֶר עָשָׂה לְנִפְלְאוֹתָיו'. בְּסֵפֶר לְזִכָּרוֹן leads to 'סֵפֶר זִכָּרוֹן' (Mal 3:16). קַהְתָּה דוֹר מֵאֶלֶף leads to 'לְאֶלֶף דּוֹר' (Ps 105:8). אַהֲבַת כְּלוּלוֹתֶיהָ leads to Jer 2:2. מְעוֹרֵר שְׁבוּעָה leads to 'נִשְׁבַּעְתָּ' (Ex 32:13). The tiavta pair's second strophe ('תְּמוּר … קָנִינוּ שֵׁנִית') leads to 'קָנִיתָ קֶּדֶם' (Ps 74:2). תְּרַפֵּק מְשׁוֹל אֶפְרַיִם / בְּשַׁעֲשׁוּעַ יֶלֶד וּבֵן יַקִּיר leads to 'הֲבֵן יַקִּיר לִי אֶפְרַיִם … יֶלֶד שַׁעֲשֻׁעִים' (Jer 31:19). The verses are a planned framework, so splitting the strophes into eight poems would break one composition.

Page layout: the strophes are set full width in large type and the verse blocks in small type with the formula inline (s284, s286, s288). On s290 the Shabbat column ends on 'כַּכָּתוּב עַל יַד נְבִיאֶךָ' and the weekday column on 'וְנֶאֱמַר'. Both lead into one full-width Jer 31:19. That shared verse is why the final formula belongs at the structural level.

whole_work_scope.verse_scope_policy: Inside efchad_bemaasai: each formula ('כַּכָּתוּב בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ', 'כַּכָּתוּב בְּדִבְרֵי קָדְשְׁךָ', 'וְנֶאֱמַר', 'כַּכָּתוּב עַל יַד נְבִיאֶךָ') plus its verse forms one bounded quote context, kept in source order. Encode the formula as recited text and the verse as a quotation with Bible @source (e.g. bible:genesis/8/1, bible:psalms/111/4-5). Do not put canonical Bible milestones there: the weekday series repeats Gen 8:1, Ex 2:24, Ps 111:4–5 and Jer 2:2, and these copies differ in print (לְעֹלָם/יִזְכֹּר versus לְעוֹלָם/יִזְכּוֹר). Keep each copy as printed. Do not give the first 'כַּכָּתוּב בְּתוֹרָתֶךָ' (before Gen 8:1) an Atah Zokher @source. It is the same piyyut formula that comes back before Ex 2:24 and Ex 32:13. Outside the poem file: Jer 31:19 (Christian numbering 31:20) is a single shared quote with source bible:jeremiah/31/19. Its two lead-ins live in the branches ('וְנֶאֱמַר' weekday, 'כַּכָּתוּב עַל יַד נְבִיאֶךָ' Shabbat). Add a note in the efchad file that the work's tenth verse comes from the shared continuation, so its scope is documented without copying the verse.

german415.text: אַן איינעם וואָכֿענטאַג ווירד היער גלייך מיט זֵכֶר א״ז״וו בעגאָננען; אַם שַׁבָּת בעטעט מאַן אַבער ערזט פֿאָלגענדעז[?punct] אונד דאַנן אֶפְחַד א״ז״וו.
german415.translation: German 'An einem Wochentag wird hier gleich mit Secher u.s.w. begonnen; am Schabbat betet man aber erst Folgendes und dann Efchad u.s.w.' = 'On a weekday one begins here directly with Zekher etc.; on Shabbat, however, one first prays the following and then Efchad etc.'
uncertainties: א״ז״וו (both times): in the Rashi-style type the first letter looks like ח and the second like ג. In this typeface those are the normal shapes of א and ז, so the reading is א״ז״וו = 'u.s.w.' (und so weiter), standard Judeo-German spelling with ז for German s. The candidate's ת״ו/ח״ו readings are wrong. The human marked this '(?)'. Record it as my reading of the glyphs, which agrees with the human's tentative one, not as a human-certain reading.

ערזט = 'erst' ('first'). It uses the same ז-for-s convention as פֿאָלגענדעז (folgendes) and makes good sense next to 'und dann'. The human marked it '(?)'. I agree with ערזט; it is still my reading, not a human certainty.
The human's two strings disagree: the 'text' field has 'אַנ' (medial nun) and 'verbatim_answer' has 'אַן'. The print has final ן.

Pointing that conflicts with the human text: in the print the zayin incipit looks like זֵכֶר (tsere-segol, the poem's incipit), not the human's זַכָר, and פֿאָלגענדעז looks like it has qamats, not patah. Both are tiny at this resolution; check them at higher zoom.
A punctuation mark (colon or semicolon) seems to follow פֿאָלגענדעז in the print. The human text has none there. Check it.

verdict: Approve the whole-work scope: one efchad_bemaasai identity and file with 46 strophes and 8 internal verse quote contexts, alongside the separate 44-strophe zekher_techillat file. One change: the final Shabbat lead-in to the shared Jer 31:19 belongs in the structural Shabbat branch. Make the weekday/Shabbat choice once, at the structural level. The earlier instruction to keep eight separate Shabbat poems is withdrawn; layout, acrostic, labels and text do not support it. All seven reuses are approved with no new identities: the brit insertion points to the ordinary stanza_1 (not the circumcision recension), and Atah Zokher gets two new internal boundaries (/opening, /vegam_et_noach), not a new identity. The German 415 reading is approved as my reading, with the human's tentative status kept. The Efchad attribution 'בראשי החרוזות' is confirmed against the image but still needs human adjudication. This is a scope and identity review only, not acceptance of the batch.
